# Migration Intentions - v1.5.1

## Intentions

<!-- boilerstone:intentions:begin — generated by `pnpm boilerplate intentions sync`, do not edit -->

- [`00-ci-skip-draft-pull-requests.md`](./00-ci-skip-draft-pull-requests.md) — `migration` · `ci` — A draft pull request gets no CI run, a new push cancels the CI run of the previous push, the PR lint runs cancel each other, and the Release note job starts a runner only on a Release PR.
- [`01-ci-cancel-superseded-main-runs.md`](./01-ci-cancel-superseded-main-runs.md) — `migration` · `ci` — A new push to `main` cancels the CI run of `main` that is still going. When several merges follow each other, only the run for the last commit finishes.
- [`02-push-after-local-gates.md`](./02-push-after-local-gates.md) — `migration` · `tooling` — The project guide tells agents to push only when lint, typecheck and the tests of the changed packages pass locally.
- [`03-release-in-batches.md`](./03-release-in-batches.md) — `migration` · `tooling` — The project's release page and its `project-release` skill say that releases ship in batches (several pull requests, then one release), give the order to follow, and warn that the release note is written or renamed last.
- [`04-release-note-holds-the-tag.md`](./04-release-note-holds-the-tag.md) — `migration` · `ci` — When `REQUIRE_RELEASE_NOTE` is `true`, the Release Please workflow creates no tag, no GitHub Release and no images for a Release PR merged without its note, and publishes the release once the note lands on `main`. When the variable is not set, the release is published with the notes release-please generates, without a red run.
- [`05-worktree-remove-promoted-intentions.md`](./05-worktree-remove-promoted-intentions.md) — `migration` · `tooling` — `pnpm worktree:remove <name>` treats a squash-merged branch as integrated even when a release has since moved the branch's unreleased intention to `vX.Y.Z/NN-<slug>.md`. — requires `v1.5.0/worktree-commands`

<!-- boilerstone:intentions:end -->
